correctness.rationale: The exact objective follows from a sixteen-subspace lattice identity and is independently replayed by a rational Markov recurrence. Explicit Hessian domination gives global curvature at least 1/10. Each of the three boundary edges has a positive denominator and a quartic/cubic numerator that is positive on the entire unit interval by 208 independently recomputed rational Bernstein coefficients. A thirteen-column rational witness is strictly better than all boundary points. Compactness and strong convexity prove existence and uniqueness of the interior minimizer. The critical system and gradient residual yield a radius smaller than 2e-9. Computation is an exact finite certificate, not extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General formulas of Wang--Yaakobi cover the objective but not the global minimum classification; a general formula can be specialized without yielding uniqueness or the strict all-face certificate. Hofmeister et al. work as information dimension tends to infinity with peeling decoding, unlike fixed dimension three with ideal span decoding. The large-field k=3 constructions of Boruchovsky et al. do not subsume the claimed binary symmetric strict-convexity theorem.

residual_risks: The strongest close source already gives the exact three-bit functional and a numerical positive-degree optimizer; novel priority is confined strictly to the rigorous uniqueness, all-boundary exclusion and certified enclosure.

value.rationale: The binary three-bit case is the smallest fully symmetric problem with three nonzero column degrees. Prior work gave a numerical candidate without a global optimizer classification. The new theorem completely identifies uniqueness and necessary support of its best distribution, separates the entire weight-deficient boundary with an exact rational gap, and gives a certified algebraic enclosure, providing genuine design information rather than an incremental numerical improvement.
